name: Lin Zhenfu
current_role: Listed as co-holder of Lin family stake in Sichuan Kexin Mechanical and Electrical Equipment (SZSE: 300092); current role unconfirmed
profile: Appeared on Hurun China 2010 alongside Lin Zhenhua and Lin Zhenrong as a shared Lin family fortune from Sichuan Kexin, a Shifang, Sichuan maker of pressure vessels (incl. nuclear-grade equipment) founded 1997 and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2010. Lin Zhenhua is chairman; no public source found naming Lin Zhenfu's own role.
interesting_fact: Sichuan Kexin is one of the few Chinese makers of nuclear-grade pressure vessel equipment.
notes: Could not find any source (English or Chinese search) naming 林祯富 individually; wealth was a shared family listing with chairman Lin Zhenhua. Best route is via the company's Shenzhen-listed IR channels / chairman Lin Zhenhua. Low priority.

name: Vikram S Shriram
current_role: Vice Chairman & Managing Director, DCM Shriram Ltd (since Sept 2001)
profile: Member of the Shriram business family, Vikram S. Shriram co-runs DCM Shriram, a Delhi-based conglomerate in chlor-alkali/vinyl chemicals, sugar, fertilisers, agri-inputs and captive power, alongside elder brother and Chairman Ajay S. Shriram. A chartered accountant, he has been Vice Chairman & MD since 2001.
interesting_fact: He is a qualified chartered accountant (Associate Member, ICAI) with a B.Com (Hons) from Calcutta University, and the company bio notes his strong aptitude for finance.
deep_cut_fact: After training across SRF Group functions, he joined Shriram Bearings Ltd in Ranchi in 1981 as senior management (works, marketing, general management); he studied at Mayo College, Ajmer, and lists swimming and cooking as hobbies.
notes: response@dcmshriram.com is the general corporate email in 2022-24 annual reports; shares@ appears in a 2022 AGM notice (shareholder services). DCM Shriram has a large captive power business - an angle for an energy podcast. Not to be confused with DCM Shriram Industries (separate company).

name: Chigurupati Krishna Prasad
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Granules India Ltd
profile: Dr. Krishna Prasad Chigurupati founded Triton Laboratories in Hyderabad in 1984 with Uma Chigurupati to make paracetamol API; it grew into Granules India, among the world's largest makers of paracetamol, metformin and ibuprofen and a pioneer of pharmaceutical formulation intermediates (PFIs). He still leads it as CMD, pushing green-chemistry projects and a 2025 move into peptides.
interesting_fact: Granules commissioned what it called the world's largest single-site PFI plant at Gagillapur in 2003; he received the Economic Times Lifetime Achievement Award (2022) and an IOD Distinguished Fellowship (2025).
deep_cut_fact: In 1987 his first company, Triton Laboratories, became only the second Indian pharma company to export to the United States; Triton also pioneered selling bulk 'direct compressible' granulated paracetamol (PFIs).
notes: Granules' 'Healthy People, Healthy Planet' green-molecules push (Granules CZRO subsidiary) is a good sustainability/energy hook. Family also active in company (Uma, Priyanka, Harsha Chigurupati are EDs).

name: Wang Mingjun
current_role: Co-founder of the Boton flavours & fragrances group (China Boton Group, HKEX: 3318); chairman at 2005 IPO, current role unconfirmed
profile: Wang Mingjun (王明均) co-founded Shenzhen Boton Flavors & Fragrances in 1991 with his brothers Wang Mingfan, Wang Mingqing and Wang Mingyou; the group listed in Hong Kong in 2005 as China Flavors and Fragrances (now China Boton Group), with him as chairman. Brother Wang Mingfan is shown as Chairman & CEO in recent (2023) filings.
interesting_fact: The Boton group researches, makes and sells flavours and fragrances in China, mostly under the 'Boton' (波頓) brand, and was listed in Hong Kong in 2005 as China Flavors and Fragrances.
deep_cut_fact: Per the 2005 Hong Kong prospectus, he joined the family venture in March 1991 and by IPO had ~20 years in flavour-and-fragrance management; the group was run by four Wang brothers.
notes: Sources conflict on who chairs China Boton today (one aggregator says Wang Mingjun chairman since 2012; 2023 pay records list brother Wang Mingfan as Chairman & CEO). Verify against latest HKEX annual report for 3318 before outreach. No published personal/office contact found.

name: Balram Garg
current_role: Managing Director, PC Jeweller Ltd (reappointed for five years, Aug 2026)
profile: Balram Garg co-founded PC Jeweller with his elder brother Padam Chand Gupta, coming from a wholesale gold-trading background; it opened its first showroom in Karol Bagh, Delhi in April 2005 and listed on NSE/BSE in December 2012. As MD he is leading a turnaround, converting promoter warrants into equity and raising promoter holding to ~39% in 2026.
interesting_fact: PC Jeweller went from a single Karol Bagh showroom in 2005 to 41 stores by March 2014 and listed after an oversubscribed 2012 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: The company was originally incorporated as 'P Chand Jewellers'; its Noida SEZ export unit won Highest Exporter and Best Exporter (gems & jewellery) awards for 2009-10 and 2010-11.
notes: Company went through a debt restructuring with lenders in recent years - avoid that topic. Corporate office is in Karol Bagh, New Delhi.

name: Rup Chand Lohia
current_role: Senior patriarch/director of the Merino Group (Merino Industries / Merino Panel Products, Kolkata); reportedly redesignated Chairman Emeritus in 2024
profile: Rup Chand Lohia is a senior member of the Lohia family behind the Kolkata-based Merino Group, one of India's largest makers of high-pressure decorative laminates, plus plywood, panels and food processing. The family business dates to 1965 (Hapur, UP); day-to-day leadership now sits with family members such as MD Prakash Lohia and CEO Manoj Lohia.
interesting_fact: Merino set up its first high-pressure decorative laminate plant at Hapur in 1981 and now runs laminate plants in Hapur, Rohad, Dahej and Hosur, among India's largest capacities.
notes: Very low public profile; Merino Industries is unlisted (CIN U51909WB1965PLC026556). 'Chairman Emeritus' (2024) came from a search summary of an annual report not directly verified. Best route is via Merino corporate office in Kolkata or MD Prakash Lohia. Alive status not confirmed (no obituary found).

name: Sevantilal Shah
current_role: Co-founder, Venus Jewel (Surat/Mumbai diamond manufacturer); trustee of Rasilaben Sevantilal Shah Venus Hospital, Surat
profile: Sevantilal Premchand Shah co-founded Venus Jewel in 1969 with elder brother Ramniklal; it became one of India's most respected diamond cutters and the first Indian firm to cut and polish 2-carat-plus stones at scale. The next generation (Anil, Rajesh, Hitesh) now runs the business while he focuses on philanthropy.
interesting_fact: Venus Jewel switched to cash-only terms when most Indian firms sold on 120-day-plus credit - a risky move that briefly dented sales until buyers came back for its cutting quality.
deep_cut_fact: After seeing patients' struggles during family hospital visits in 2016, he envisioned 'a hospital that runs on ethical grounds'; Venus Jewel put ~$6M into the Smt Rasilaben Sevantilal Shah Venus Hospital in Surat, opened in 2019 with PM Modi attending; ~70 Venus staff help run it.
notes: Received GJEPC Lifetime Achievement Award (March 2017). Elderly; alive status not confirmed but no obituary found. Country field empty in input - he is Indian (Surat). Best route likely via Venus Jewel / nephew Hitesh Shah. No published contact verified (company site unreachable).

name: Thomas J. Healy
current_role: Founder & CEO, Hyliion Holdings Corp. (HYLN)
profile: Thomas Healy founded Hyliion in 2015 out of Carnegie Mellon to electrify long-haul trucks and took it public via SPAC in Oct 2020 at a $1B+ valuation. After exiting the EV powertrain business in 2023, he pivoted Hyliion to the KARNO generator - a 3D-printed, fuel-agnostic linear-heat generator (tech bought from GE for $37M) pitched for data centers, the US Navy and oilfield power.
interesting_fact: He argues 'every electron will end up in a data center' and that providers now start site planning with 'How do we secure power?' rather than 'Where do we put servers?' - a direct fit for an energy/data-center podcast.
deep_cut_fact: A Carnegie Mellon mechanical engineering & public policy grad (ENG 2014) with a passion for racing and motorsports, he founded two startups while still in college before starting Hyliion from his CMU dorm room; CMU featured him in its 'Tartans on the Rise' alumni honours.
notes: Top-priority guest for the podcast: young founder now selling on-site generators to data centers (Flexnode LOI for up to 10 KARNO units, US Navy and Air Force contracts). Does media readily (FreightWaves, Startup Junkie podcast). Forbes 30 Under 30 (2017).

name: D. Scott Barbour
current_role: President & CEO, Advanced Drainage Systems (WMS) since Sept 2017; Director, Allison Transmission (since 2022)
profile: Scott Barbour runs Advanced Drainage Systems, the Ohio-based leader in thermoplastic corrugated pipe and stormwater/on-site septic solutions, much of it made from recycled plastic. Before ADS he spent 27 years at Emerson Electric, latterly running Emerson Network Power, the data-center power and cooling business sold in 2016 and renamed Vertiv.
interesting_fact: Under Barbour, ADS leans heavily on recycled plastic - by 2019 about 65% of its pipes were made from recycled materials - and in 2026 it closed the acquisition of National Diversified Sales from Norma Group.
deep_cut_fact: Before ADS he spent 27 years at Emerson Electric and helped sell its Network Power business (now Vertiv); he says he learned board communication watching Emerson CEO David Farr, and still had monthly lunches with his ADS predecessor Joe Chlapaty.
notes: Strong data-center angle via his Emerson Network Power/Vertiv history. Education: BSME Southern Methodist University, MBA Vanderbilt Owen. IR contact is Michael Higgins, VP Corporate Strategy & IR.

name: Maamoun Rajeh
current_role: President, Arch Capital Group Ltd (since Nov 2024; remit widened June 2026 to Insurance, Reinsurance and Mortgage)
profile: Maamoun Rajeh is a founding member of Arch Capital's 2001 relaunch, starting as an underwriter at Arch Re Bermuda and rising through CEO of Arch Re Europe, CEO of Arch Re Bermuda and Chairman/CEO of Arch Worldwide Reinsurance Group (2017-24). As President he now oversees all three operating segments of the Bermuda-based (re)insurer under CEO Nicolas Papadopoulo.
interesting_fact: Before Arch he spent about a decade in strategic planning and underwriting at USF&G, F&G Re and Hartford Re; in April 2026 he joined the steering committee of the Insurance Development Forum (UN/World Bank-linked risk-finance partnership).
deep_cut_fact: He was named a gala honoree of Ronald McDonald House New York, recognised alongside his roles chairing Somers Group Holdings and serving on the Global Reinsurance Forum.
notes: Wharton graduate. Press contact is Greg Hare (Arch media relations). Insurance/reinsurance angle: catastrophe and energy-infrastructure risk.

name: Charles Alan Williams
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Northpointe Bancshares, Inc. (NYSE: NPB) and CEO/director of Northpointe Bank, Grand Rapids, MI
profile: Charles 'Chuck' Williams founded Northpointe Bank in Grand Rapids in 1998-99 after a decade as SVP and senior lending officer at First National Bank of America. He built it into one of the only mortgage-focused banks in the US and one of the largest providers of mortgage warehouse financing, taking the holding company public on the NYSE in 2025.
interesting_fact: Northpointe operates nationally from a single Grand Rapids headquarters, describing itself as one of the largest mortgage warehouse lenders and one of the only mortgage-focused banks in the country.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Northpointe he spent 1988-1997 as SVP, senior lending officer and director at First National Bank of America (formerly First National Bank of Michigan), serving on its executive committee; he is a graduate of the University of Wisconsin's Graduate School of Banking.
notes: Press-release contacts are CFO Brad Howes (IR) and President Kevin Comps. Over 42 years in banking. Limited fit to energy/data-center theme; entrepreneurship (bank founder) angle.

name: Peter J Millones
current_role: Executive Vice President & General Counsel, Booking Holdings Inc. (BKNG)
profile: Peter Millones has been Booking Holdings' (formerly Priceline.com) top lawyer since January 2001 and an EVP since 2003, leading legal, compliance and privacy for the parent of Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, Kayak and OpenTable. He joined Priceline in March 2000 from Latham & Watkins as VP and Associate General Counsel, during the dot-com era.
interesting_fact: He has been general counsel of the same company for 25+ years - from Priceline.com in 2001 through its transformation into Booking Holdings - an unusually long tenure for a Fortune 500 GC; he is profiled by Chambers as an in-house leader.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Priceline.com in March 2000 - at the very peak of the dot-com bubble - leaving Latham & Watkins to become VP & Associate GC, and was promoted to General Counsel within ten months.
notes: Executive, not a founder; low public profile. Best route is Booking Holdings media relations (communications@). Weak fit for an entrepreneurship/energy podcast.

name: Peter Nieh
current_role: Co-founder & Partner, Lightspeed Venture Partners
profile: Peter Nieh co-founded Lightspeed Venture Partners and has ~30 years in venture, mainly SaaS and infrastructure. His 10%-owner SEC filings for Rubrik and Netskope reflect Lightspeed fund holdings (Lightspeed led Rubrik's 2014 Series A and is its largest holder). Past investments include DoubleClick, Informatica, Blue Nile, Nest, QuantumScape and Eightfold.
interesting_fact: His portfolio spans energy and hardware as well as software - he is listed as an investor in solid-state battery maker QuantumScape and in Nest, the smart-thermostat company Google bought for $3.2B.
deep_cut_fact: He entered venture in 1995 after working in business development and product marketing at General Magic, the legendary Apple spin-off that built an early handheld communicator; outside work he plays competitive ultimate frisbee.
notes: Stanford BA and MBA. Good energy angle via QuantumScape and Nest; Lightspeed is a large AI/infra investor. VC so reachable via Lightspeed; X handle @peterlsvp.

name: Mark David Jenkins
current_role: Co-President and Head of Global Credit & Insurance, The Carlyle Group (since Jan 2026); member of Carlyle Leadership Committee
profile: Mark Jenkins joined Carlyle in 2016 to lead its global credit business after heading the Global Private Investment group at Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPPIB). He now runs Global Credit & Insurance and was named Co-President from January 2026. Earlier he spent 11 years at Goldman Sachs and was co-head of leveraged finance origination at Barclays Capital.
interesting_fact: At CPPIB he founded CPPIB Credit Investments and led the pension fund's acquisition of GE's Antares Capital middle-market lending business, then oversaw its expansion.
deep_cut_fact: A Queen's University B.Comm grad, he has sat on an unusually varied set of boards - including Teine Energy, reinsurers Wilton Re and Fortitude Re, and Antares Capital - spanning credit, insurance and energy.
notes: Based in New York. Carlyle media contact Brittany Bensaull (Global Head of Corporate Communications) per 2026 releases. Energy angle via Teine Energy board and Carlyle's infrastructure/energy credit financing.

name: Igor Tadeusz Kuzniar
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Partner / CIO, Teleios Capital Partners (Zug, Switzerland)
profile: Igor Kuzniar, a Swiss citizen, co-founded Teleios Capital in Zug in 2013, a concentrated, engaged-ownership investor in European small- and mid-cap equities. Through Teleios funds he holds ~10% of Quanex Building Products (NYSE: NX), with board-observer rights. Earlier he was a Managing Director at Octavian Advisors (2006-12) and worked at McKinsey.
interesting_fact: Teleios is regulated by both the US SEC and Swiss FINMA and runs a deliberately concentrated portfolio, building close relationships with boards to influence governance and capital allocation.
deep_cut_fact: He served as a non-executive director of UK household and personal-care products maker McBride plc (2019-2023); academically he studied at St. Gallen, LSE and Harvard Business School.
notes: Activist/engaged investor; media enquiries go via Greenbrook PR. Education/career details are from MarketScreener aggregator - verify. Limited energy fit; investing/entrepreneurship angle.

name: Timothy Lain
current_role: Senior Vice President & Chief Financial Officer, Carpenter Technology Corp. (CRS), since Aug 2020
profile: Tim Lain is CFO of Carpenter Technology, the Pennsylvania maker of specialty alloys (nickel and cobalt superalloys, titanium) for aerospace, defense, medical and energy markets. He joined Carpenter in 2007 after 12 years at McGladrey & Pullen (now RSM), serving as VP-Controller/CAO (2013-18), VP & CFO (2018-20) and SVP & CFO since Aug 2020.
interesting_fact: Carpenter announced an additional $1.0 billion share repurchase program in August 2026 after completing its prior authorization, reflecting strong cash generation from aerospace and defense alloy demand.
deep_cut_fact: Before industry he spent about 12 years (1995-2007) in public accounting at McGladrey & Pullen, rising to Audit Director; he is a graduate of Temple University's Fox School of Business.
notes: Corporate CFO, not a founder. Carpenter IR (John Huyette, +1 610-208-2061) and media (Heather Beardsley) contacts are phone-only in releases; no published email found. Energy angle: superalloys for gas turbines used in power generation.

name: Robert P Ragusa
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, GRAIL, Inc. (GRAL) since Oct 2021; Director, Twist Bioscience
profile: Bob Ragusa leads GRAIL, the multi-cancer early-detection company behind the Galleri blood test, which was spun out of Illumina as an independent Nasdaq company in 2024. An operations executive, he was Illumina's COO / SVP Global Quality & Operations for about eight years and earlier ran global operations and service at radiation-oncology firm Accuray. In 2026 GRAIL filed Galleri's FDA premarket approval application.
interesting_fact: Under Ragusa GRAIL submitted an FDA premarket approval application for its Galleri multi-cancer early detection test (Jan 2026), took a $110M equity investment from Samsung entities (June 2026) and went before an FDA advisory committee in Sept 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Before GRAIL he was EVP Global Operations & Service at Accuray, maker of the CyberKnife radiosurgery system, then spent ~8 years running Illumina's operations; Illumina's CEO cited his 'strong track record of execution' when naming him GRAIL CEO.
notes: Health/biotech rather than energy. GRAIL comms contacts: Kristen Davis, Trish Rowland (pr@grail.com).

name: Peter Benjamin
current_role: Senior Executive Vice President & Group President, The TJX Companies (oversees Marmaxx: T.J. Maxx, Marshalls, Sierra)
profile: Peter Benjamin is a 35-year TJX veteran who rose through merchandising: he started at Marshalls in 1990, spent six years as Chief Merchandising Officer of Marmaxx, became Marmaxx President in 2023 and Group President/SEVP in 2025. Marmaxx is the largest US off-price apparel and home-fashions division.
interesting_fact: He has spent essentially his whole career in off-price retail, joining Marshalls in 1990 - before TJX acquired Marshalls in 1995 - and eventually running the combined T.J. Maxx/Marshalls division.
deep_cut_fact: He began in retail through the executive training program at Boston department store Filene's, where he worked as a buyer before joining Marshalls; he also serves as a trustee of Save the Children US.
notes: Corporate executive, low public profile. TJX press releases list only a phone contact (Debra McConnell, Global Communications); no press email found. Weak fit for energy/data-center theme.

name: Peter Kamin
current_role: Founder & Managing Partner, 3K Limited Partnership (family investment partnership); Chairman, Tile Shop Holdings; Director, Psychemedics
profile: Peter H. Kamin co-founded activist investor ValueAct Capital in 2000 with Jeffrey Ubben and George Hamel, serving as a founding member and Managing Partner for about 11 years. Since 2012 he has invested through his own family partnership, 3K, taking concentrated stakes and board seats - chairing Tile Shop (~17% holder) and backing Psychemedics' 2024 going-private transaction.
interesting_fact: He was one of the three co-founders of ValueAct Capital, the San Francisco activist fund later famous for winning a Microsoft board seat in 2013.
deep_cut_fact: Before ValueAct he founded Peak Investment LP in 1992, and he has served on small-cap boards as varied as Calloway's Nursery, Rand Worldwide and golf-shaft maker Aldila.
notes: Private investor; 3K states it has no business phone. Tile Shop delisted/deregistered from Nasdaq in late 2025, so IR channel may be limited. Peak Investment and board history come from MarketScreener aggregator - verify. Do not use the filing address (residential/office mix).

name: Sean P Hennessy
current_role: Independent Director, TransDigm Group (since 2006, audit chair) and Perimeter Solutions (since 2021); retired Sherwin-Williams CFO
profile: Sean Hennessy, a CPA and University of Akron graduate (1980), spent his career at Sherwin-Williams, serving as CFO from 2001 to 2016 and then as SVP Corporate Planning, Development & Administration, leading the integration of the $9.3B Valspar acquisition until 2018. He now serves on the boards of aerospace-parts maker TransDigm and fire-retardant/specialty-chemicals company Perimeter Solutions.
interesting_fact: He was Sherwin-Williams' CFO for about 15 years and then led integration of the $9.3B Valspar acquisition (closed June 2017), which Sherwin-Williams said created the global leader in paint and coatings.
deep_cut_fact: Perimeter Solutions, where he is a director, makes Phos-Chek - the world's most-used wildfire retardant, applied from air tankers and helicopters; he has also sat on TransDigm's board since 2006.
notes: Retired executive/board member; no published personal contact. Approach via TransDigm or Perimeter Solutions IR. Bio details come largely from aggregator profiles - verify against TDG/PRM proxy statements.
